market.headline: Stocks fell about 2% on Thursday for a sixth straight loss, and Nasdaq futures are down another 1.5% this morning.
points: Thursday: The S&P 500 fell 2.0%, the Nasdaq 2.3% and the Dow 2.2%, or about 1,100 points. Ten of the 11 market groups fell. Health care dropped another 2% and household goods stocks about 1.5%.

Chips: Nvidia fell 3.3% to a new 52-week low. AMD sank 7.7% after a short seller (an investor who bets a stock will fall) said AMD has its own China problems. AMD says the claims are wrong. Taiwan's market fell 4.4%.
Anthropic closed its first day at $97.17, up 17% from its $83 IPO price, but it is down about 6% to 10% before Friday's open. The fear gauge (VIX) jumped to about 28, its highest since March.

Rates: Traders see about a 96% chance the Fed raises rates on Dec 9. The 10-year US bond yield eased a bit to 5.04%. Next week is short: US markets close Thursday for American Thanksgiving and close early Friday.
market.plan: This is a week to protect cash, not chase dips. Don't buy anything new today. If you add money, stick to the calm Canadian halal fund in small pieces and let the selling settle before touching tech.

stocks.sum: The simple, certified way to own about 220 halal US companies at once.
why: One purchase spreads your money over many companies, so one bad stock hurts less.
Certified halal, so there is no screening homework.
It was already about 10% below its high on Nov 17, and the market has fallen more since then.
risk: The S&P 500 has now fallen six days in a row, including 2% on Thursday. Nvidia and Apple are a big part of this fund, and tech is leading the drop.
Futures point to another down day, and the fear gauge is the highest since March.
I could not confirm a close after Nov 17, so the price shown is from then and is likely lower now. Check the live price in your app.
stocks.todo: Still the best long-term first purchase on this list, but pause for a few days. When the market has a couple of calm or up days in a row, start with a small first piece.

stocks.sum: A calm, Canadian-dollar halal fund. No currency fee when you buy it.
why: Trades in Canadian dollars, so you skip the 1.5% US currency fee each way.
Holds steady companies around the world and moves much less than tech.
Certified halal.
risk: World markets fell hard this week, including a 4.4% drop in Taiwan on Thursday, so expect it to be a bit lower than the price shown.
Slow mover. Good for safety, weak for quick gains.
I could not confirm a close after Nov 17.
stocks.todo: Still the one buy on this list, but only in small pieces. Split what you plan to put in into three or four buys over the next couple of weeks, and use a limit order at or a little under the live price.

stocks.n: SP Funds Dow Jones Global Sukuk ETF
stocks.sum: A halal income fund that pays monthly, about 4.9% a year. Not a growth play.
why: Pays a small amount every month.
Barely moves when stocks drop.
risk: It sits very close to its 52-week low of $17.30. The Fed looks almost certain to raise rates on Dec 9, and funds like this tend to drift lower when rates rise.
US withholding tax takes 15% of the payouts inside an FHSA.
I could not confirm a close after Nov 17.
stocks.todo: Only use it to park cash for income. It will not help a few-month profit goal, and rising rates are a headwind right now.

stocks.earnNote: Broadcom, a big holding, reports Dec 9
stocks.sum: The chip rebound trade without leverage, spread over 26 chip makers.
why: About a third below its high, so there is room to recover once the selling stops.
Owning a basket means one company's bad news, like AMD's on Thursday, hurts less than owning that stock alone.
risk: It fell 2.6% on Thursday and moves almost twice as much as the market.

Chip stocks are being hit from all sides: the new US chip export rules, a short seller's report on AMD, Nvidia's leadership mess and a 4.4% drop in Taiwan. Chip makers are down again before Friday's open.
Broadcom, a big holding, reports Dec 9.
stocks.todo: Keep waiting. Look again once chips stop making new lows for at least a week, and think about one share at most.

stocks.sum: The AI chip leader. Strong results, but the stock keeps falling on worries about who runs it.
why: Sales roughly doubled from a year ago to about $116 billion.
Cheap against its profits for a company growing this fast. Its price-to-earnings is about 16.
risk: It fell 3.3% on Thursday to a new 52-week low, its sixth loss in a row. It gave up an early gain of almost 5%.
Former CEO Jensen Huang faces closed-door interviews with Congress on Dec 1, and a shareholder lawsuit is pending. Daiwa cut its price target to $185.
It moves more than twice as much as the market, and the new US chip export rules add more uncertainty.
stocks.todo: Keep waiting. A stock that keeps falling after good results is telling you the worry isn't over. Look again after the Dec 1 hearings or when a new CEO is named.

stocks.sum: A big winner from custom AI chips, about 28% below its high.
why: Analysts' average target is well above the price.
It held up better than most chip names this week. It is about flat since Nov 13.
risk: It fell about 2.1% on Thursday and is down about 3% before Friday's open.
Its own earnings on Dec 9 are the next big test, less than three weeks away.
One firm recently cut its rating and target to $398, so not everyone agrees with the average target.
stocks.todo: Keep waiting while chips are this jumpy. If you buy later, plan to be out or smaller before Dec 9.

stocks.sum: Strong business, but the wildest stock on this list, and now facing a short seller.
why: Record quarter on Nov 3, and analysts still mostly rate it a buy.
risk: It sank 7.7% on Thursday after Hunterbrook, a short seller, said AMD chip software kept showing up in products from a Chinese server maker on the US blacklist. AMD says it follows US export law. It is down about 5% to 6% more before Friday's open.
It moves two and a half times as much as the market.
Very expensive against current profits, so bad news hits it hard.
stocks.todo: Skip it for now. A normal stop can't protect you on a stock that swings this much, and the China question needs to be answered first.

stocks.sum: Makes the chips for nearly every AI company, so it wins whoever leads.
why: Makes the chips almost every AI company needs, and it just reported a record month of sales.
Analysts' average target is far above the price.
risk: It closed at $352.09 on Thursday, down about 12% in four trading days. Taiwan's main market fell 4.4% the same day.
Reports say TSMC and Samsung paused some chip shipments to Chinese customers under the new US rule.
Taiwan and US-China politics are a standing risk. The Trump and Xi talks in Shenzhen ended with little change on chips.
stocks.todo: Keep waiting. Look again once the price holds steady for a week and the chip rule news settles.

stocks.sum: The steady one in tech, but software stocks are still shaky.
why: About 11% below its high, a smaller drop than most of tech.
Moves about the same as the market, so the stop can be tighter.
Microsoft has published its review of last week's outage. It blamed a hidden bug from an earlier network change.
risk: It fell about 2% on Thursday with the rest of big tech and is now under $500.
Software stocks are still under pressure from fears that AI tools will replace some software.
One share is about $700 CAD, a big piece of a small account.
stocks.todo: Still wait. The outage news is out of the way, but the whole market is sliding. If it steadies for a few days, a limit order for one share is fair.

stocks.sum: The cheapest big tech name against its profits, about 31% below its high.
why: Its price-to-earnings is near 15, which is low for a big tech company. That means you pay less for each dollar of profit.
Its income comes from ads and cloud, so it depends less on chip spending.
It owns a big stake in Anthropic, which closed its first day 17% above its IPO price.
risk: It jumped early Thursday but closed down 3.5%, giving back all its Anthropic gains. Anthropic is down again before Friday's open.
It sits less than 1% above its 52-week low. Cheap stocks can get cheaper.
Investors still worry about how much it is spending on AI.
stocks.todo: Keep waiting. Watch whether it holds above its 52-week low near $271. If it breaks below, give it more time.

stocks.sum: A safe haven lately, but priced at the top.
why: Investors have treated it as a safe spot during the chip selloff. It fell only 0.9% on Thursday while the Nasdaq fell 2.3%.
risk: Still only about 3% below its all-time high and above analysts' average target.
Pricey against profits, so there is little room left for a few-month trade.
stocks.todo: Hold off. Put it on your list for a pullback of 8% or more.

stocks.sum: A story stock. The price runs on headlines more than on profits.
why: About 25% below its high.
risk: It fell 2.4% on Thursday with the rest of tech.
Extremely expensive against its profits.
It swings on headlines like robotaxi news, a possible SpaceX tie-up and China sales more than on actual profits.
stocks.todo: Skip for a planned, rule-based trade. Too unpredictable.

stocks.sum: Reasonably priced and about 24% below its high, but the halal status needs your own check.
why: Fair price against profits, and analysts' target is well above today's price.
risk: Halal screeners do not all agree on Meta. Check Zoya or Musaffa first.
It fell 3.3% on Thursday and is borrowing heavily to pay for AI.
Italy fined it about $887 million last week over how it used phone photos.
stocks.todo: Settle the halal question first. If it passes for you, look again once big tech stops sliding.

stocks.sum: The weight-loss drug leader, about 5% below a record high.
why: Not a tech stock, so it spreads your risk.
It usually moves much less than the market.
risk: Health stocks fell again on Thursday, down about 2% as a group, over the US Medicare audit plan. That fight could drag on until comments close in January.
Still expensive against profits and close to analysts' average target.
One share costs about $1,950 CAD. I could not confirm Thursday's close, so the price shown is from Nov 18.
stocks.todo: Hold off. Too big for one share on a $10,000 account, and the dip is small so far.

stocks.sum: A defensive stock that investors ran to during the tech selloff.
why: Very calm. It usually hardly reacts to market drops.
risk: It fell more than 2% again on Thursday with other health stocks. I could not confirm the exact close, so the price shown is from Nov 18.
It is still near analysts' average target, so there is little room left.
The talc lawsuits are still ongoing.
stocks.todo: Hold off. Good company, but you would still be buying near the top of its run.

stocks.sum: A calm health care name about 21% below its high. It held up well on a rough day.
why: It held up well on Wednesday while health care fell.
A discount without tech's wild swings, and steady product news.
A low share price means you can buy several shares and size the trade exactly.
risk: Health care fell another 2% as a group on Thursday. I could not confirm Abbott's close, so the price shown is from Nov 18.
The US Medicare audit plan is weighing on the whole health group, and that news is not settled.
stocks.todo: Still wait. Two down days in a row for health care is not a calm setup. If it holds steady into next week, buying in one go would be fair.

stocks.sum: Soap, diapers and razors. Steady, but near its high.
why: People buy its products in any economy, and it just raised its dividend for the 70th year in a row.
At Thursday's investor day it laid out a plan to save up to $10 billion by 2030, partly by cutting 20% to 30% of its factory and supply jobs as it adds automation.
risk: It closed at about $171.72 on Nov 17, close to its high. I could not confirm a US close since then.
Household goods stocks fell about 1.5% on Thursday, so even safe names are slipping.
stocks.todo: Hold off. Useful as a safe corner later, not as a profit trade now.

stocks.sum: Beat forecasts this week and named a new CEO, but the stock keeps drifting lower.
why: Sales and profit came in a little above forecasts, and it kept its full-year plan.
Fair price against profits, and older US homes need repairs.
risk: The finance chief, Richard McPhail, takes over as CEO on Monday, Nov 23. Leadership changes can bring new plans and surprises.
High rates slow home sales and big renovations, and a December Fed hike looks almost certain.
I could not confirm Thursday's close, so the price shown is from Nov 18.
stocks.todo: Let the new CEO start and the market stop sliding before buying.

stocks.sum: Sells gases that factories and hospitals need every day. Quiet and steady.
why: Calmer than the market, and nothing to do with the AI trade, so it spreads your risk.
It has raised its dividend for decades, which signals a stable business.
About 7% below its high as of Nov 18.
risk: Ten of the 11 market groups fell on Thursday, so even quiet stocks are slipping. I could not confirm Linde's close, so the price shown is from Nov 18.
One share is about $720 CAD, and the gap to analysts' target is small, so expect slow gains.
stocks.todo: Moved to wait for now. It is still a fair first stock outside tech, but let the market find its footing first. If it holds steady for a few days, a limit order for one share a little under the last price is fair.
